data.one_liner: An implementation of the Optional type to help avoid null reference errors.
data.what_it_does: Wraps values in an Optional object to explicitly track whether a value is present or absent. It provides map, filter, and conditional methods to chain operations and eliminate repetitive null checks.
use_when: You want to avoid deeply nested null-check conditionals in your Dart code.
You prefer an explicit Optional-based functional style inspired by Java's Optional.
avoid_when: You are fully satisfied with Dart's built-in sound null safety and null-aware operators (??, ?., etc.).
strengths: Helps eliminate repetitive null checks cleanly.
Implements the Iterable interface for collection compatibility.
weaknesses: Dart natively supports sound null safety, making a separate Optional library largely redundant for modern codebases.
Adds wrapper overhead for simple nullable values.
